title: [Chapitre] IV. Analysis situs (première mouture) : notes manuscrites (10/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (pp. 55-58): Grothendieck is building an axiomatic 'analysis situs' of figures. There is a set 𝓕 of figures, ordered by ≤ ('sub-figure'). The 'multiplicities' (irreducible figures) form a poset M. Each figure F is encoded by a subset F̄ of M that is closed for the order of M, i.e. a down-set; closed sets are those of the Alexandrov topology. Two figures are compatible when their sup F∪G exists. They are disjoint when they are compatible and F̄∩Ḡ=∅.

Top of the page (completing p.56). For disjoint figures F and G, the map (F',G') ↦ F'∪G' gives an isomorphism of ordered sets 𝓕_{≤F} × 𝓕_{≤G} ≅ 𝓕_{≤F∪G}. The parenthesis gives the inverse: a sub-figure H of F∪G goes to (H∩F, H∩G). He notes this is the germ of a notion of 'configurations', a family of figures in a loose sense.

'Distributivité'. In the down-set model the statement is transparent. Suppose x∈F̄, y∈Ḡ and x≤y. Then x∈Ḡ, since Ḡ is a down-set, contradicting disjointness. So no order relations link F̄ and Ḡ, and M_{≤F∪G} is the ordered sum (coproduct of posets) of M_{≤F} and M_{≤G}. Down-sets of a coproduct are pairs of down-sets. This is the poset form of 'slices over a coproduct are products of slices', i.e. disjoint and universal sums (extensivity).

'Remarque' (from the back-and-forth of p.55). The structure 𝓕 is equivalent to a family 𝔉 of closed (down-)subsets of M such that:
- (a) 𝔉 is closed under passing to closed subsets;
- (b) ⋃𝔉 = M, which given (a) is equivalent to every principal down-set M_{≤x} lying in 𝔉;
- (c) ∅ ∈ 𝔉, which given (a) is equivalent to 𝔉 ≠ ∅, and is automatic from (b) when M ≠ ∅.
So 𝔉 is a down-closed family of down-sets of M containing all principal ideals.

NB: a Galois-type bijection. On one side, the 'closed' subsets of 𝔉 (stable under sub-figures and, presumably, existing unions). On the other, the closed subsets of M. φ(𝔉') = 𝔉'∩M, identifying M with the principal figures. ψ(M') = {F∈𝔉 : F⊂M'}. These are claimed to be mutually inverse.

Next page: axiom C3 says F and G are compatible iff every X∈F is compatible with every Y∈G. This makes compatibility binary.

Taken together, 𝔉 is combinatorially the set of configurations of a 'prime event structure' (a poset of events with a binary consistency relation, configurations being down-closed consistent sets). Equivalently, when M is discrete, it is the set of cliques of a coherence space.
errors: The NB bijection needs the left-hand side to consist of sub-families of 𝔉 that are stable under sub-figures AND under existing unions (saturated). For merely down-closed sub-families of 𝔉, ψ∘φ is not the identity. The qualifying condition is illegible in the manuscript, so this is a gap in the record rather than certainly an error.
Equivalence (b) ⇔ (∀x, M_{≤x}∈𝔉) requires condition (a), which he notes. Equivalence (c) ⇔ 𝔉≠∅ also requires (a). Both are correct as stated with the 'compte tenu de' clauses.

The product decomposition uses that F̄ and Ḡ are disjoint down-sets, which forces no order relations between them. This is fine, but it requires that F∪G is represented by F̄∪Ḡ (the sup is the union of the down-sets). This is implicit from p.56 rather than proved here.

ideas.what: For disjoint compatible figures, sub-figures of F∪G correspond bijectively to pairs of sub-figures ('distributivité').
ideas.modern_name: Extensivity / disjoint universal coproducts; down-sets of a poset coproduct form a product of lattices
ideas.usually_credited_to: Disjoint universal sums: Giraud axioms in SGA4 (Grothendieck school, 1960s); extensive categories: Carboni–Lack–Walters (1993)
ideas.where_published: SGA4 Exposé IV (Giraud's characterization: sums disjoint and universal), in the topos setting rather than this poset one

ideas.what: Encoding a 'space of figures' as a down-closed family 𝔉 of down-sets of a poset M of multiplicities, containing ∅ and all principal down-sets M_{≤x}.
ideas.modern_name: Abstract simplicial complex generalized to posets / configurations of an event structure / ideal of closed sets in an Alexandrov space
ideas.usually_credited_to: Event structures: Nielsen–Plotkin–Winskel (1981); coherence spaces: Girard (1987); simplicial complexes: classical

ideas.what: Correspondence between closed sub-families of 𝔉 and closed (down-)subsets of M via φ(𝔉')=𝔉'∩M and ψ(M')={F : F⊂M'}.
ideas.modern_name: Galois connection / restriction of a structure to a sub-poset (sub-event-structure)

missed.claim: The axioms here (down-closed family of down-sets of a poset, covering by principal ideals) together with C3 on p.58 (binary compatibility: F,G compatible iff all their elements are pairwise compatible) amount to the configuration domain of a prime event structure with binary consistency. Equivalently, for discrete M, they give the cliques of a Girard coherence space. The 'distributivity' 𝓕_{≤F}×𝓕_{≤G} ≅ 𝓕_{≤F∪G} is the parallel-composition / product law for configurations. Grothendieck even uses the word 'configurations'. This is an independent 1986 appearance, in a geometric 'analysis situs' context, of structures being developed simultaneously in concurrency theory and linear logic. The two lines have not been linked.
missed.quote: la donnée de 𝔉 équivaut à un ens de parties fermées de M, satisfaisant a) ... b) ⋃_{A∈𝔉} A = M ... c) ∅∈𝔉
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical interest. It suggests his combinatorial models of 'figures' could be read with event-structure/domain-theoretic tools (stable domains, dI-domains), but it is a convergence rather than a new theorem.

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains routine order-theoretic verifications: down-sets of a poset coproduct, and an equivalent axiomatization of a family of down-sets. The only notable point is the unremarked coincidence with event structures and coherence spaces, which is mild.
transcription_corrections: Line under the arrow: it reads 'ss-fig H de F∪G' (with 'de F∪G = H' or similar), not '= M'. The parenthesis reads '(On n'a pas pris F', G' : parties de H' = F'∪G' ... H∩F et H∩G)'. So 'M'' should be 'H'' and 'M∩F', 'M∩G' should be 'H∩F', 'H∩G'. This gives the inverse map H ↦ (H∩F, H∩G).
'M_{≤F∨G}' is written with a ∨/∪ (the sup); the identification is with the 'ensemble ordonné somme' (disjoint ordered sum) of M_{≤F} and M_{≤G}.
In the 'Remarque', the first version of b) ('∅∈𝔉 (⇔ 𝔉≠∅, compte tenu de a))') is struck out and moved to c), as the transcription indicates.
NB: the left side is 𝒫_f(𝔉) (closed sub-families of 𝔉, 'qui sont stables par ...'). The condition after 'stables par' is illegible, possibly 'sous-figures et réunions'.
